newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission asks Italy to clarify milk aid plans.
newsitem.headline: Commission asks Italy to clarify milk aid plans.

text.p: The European Commission has asked Italy to clarify its plans to aid Italian dairy farmers fined 190 million Ecus for exceeding EU 1995/96 milk production quotas, a Commission spokesman said on Tuesday.
The spokesman, commenting after a meeting between EU farm Commissioner Franz Fischler and Italian farm minister Michele Pinto, said the issue was still open.

"Fischler has asked the minister for formal clarification in writing of the Italian proposal to use national funds foreseen as income support for beef producers to help its dairy sector," the spokesman said.

National income aid was allowed in addition to an 850- million-Ecu EU finance package agreed by ministers last year to provide support for beef producers facing acute problems because of the mad cow disease crisis.
Pinto has sent a letter setting out his request to be allowed to use part of Italy's share of some 33 million Ecus to give income support to dairy farmers.

Italian farmers, demonstrating against EU milk quotas, lifted on Monday a four-day blockade of roads leading to Milan's main airport on Monday after Prime Minister Romano Prodi promised to hear their grievances.
Italian dairy farmers have been protesting over the impact of a so-called super-levy of 190 million Ecus for overproducing milk by some 400,000 tonnes on a national quota of 9.9 million tonnes.

"The Italian government is barred from paying the levy on behalf of its farmers and they are not proposing to do so. Minister Pinto has suggested that he wants to pay income support under the beef crisis relief scheme," the spokesman said.
On Monday, Fischler told a news conference, after a meeting of EU farm ministers, that any review of the Italian milk quota could only be done in the context of an overall EU milk quota review.
